chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Maythamī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Yazīd, from ʿUbaydah ibn Bashīr al-Khathʿamī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the highway robber, and I said: The people say that the Imam has discretion regarding him, whatever he does.
He said: “It is not that he does whatever he wishes; rather, he deals with them according to the measure of their crimes.”

Then he said: “Whoever cuts off the road, then kills and takes wealth, his hand and foot are cut off and he is crucified. Whoever cuts off the road and kills but does not take wealth is killed. Whoever cuts off the road and takes wealth but does not kill, his hand and foot are cut off. And whoever cuts off the road and neither takes wealth nor kills is banished from the land.”

key_terms.أَخَذَ الْمَالَ: seized or stole property from victims
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the legitimate authority who implements the legal ruling
key_terms.جِنَايَاتِهِمْ: their crimes and offenses, measured according to severity
key_terms.قَاطِعِ الطَّرِيقِ: a highway robber or bandit who assaults people on the road
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ وَرِجْلُهُ: his hand and foot are cut off as a prescribed punishment
key_terms.نُفِيَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ: he is exiled or banished from the land

ai.seo_question: What punishment does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام prescribe for highway robbery in different cases?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal rulings for highway robbery based on the severity of the offender’s actions. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rejects unrestricted judicial discretion and explains that punishment is assigned in proportion to the crime committed.
